findings.title: New abstract order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `int order()` is added as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface. Any third-party or out-of-tree implementation (e.g. custom crypto providers shipped by adapters or downstream projects) will fail to compile and will throw AbstractMethodError at runtime after upgrade. Since a sensible fallback exists, this should be a `default int order() { return 100; }` (or similar) to preserve binary/source compatibility.

findings.title: Ambiguous provider selection when orders are equal is now silent
findings.body: Previously multiple CryptoProviders on the classpath caused an IllegalStateException. Now providers are sorted by order and the first is chosen; if two providers share the same order (all in-tree providers use 200, e.g. DefaultCryptoProvider, FIPS1402Provider, WildFlyElytronProvider), the selection depends on ServiceLoader iteration order and is effectively non-deterministic, with only a debug log. A conflicting FIPS/non-FIPS selection would be a silent, hard-to-diagnose misconfiguration; consider logging a warning (or failing) when the top two providers have equal order.

findings.title: logger.debugf called with a dynamically built string as format
findings.body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-constructed string as the format argument with no parameters. If any class name (or future content) contains a `%` sequence, formatting will fail/produce garbage. Use `logger.debug(builder.toString())` instead.

findings.title: Indefinite length (-1) leads to NegativeArraySizeException instead of IOException
findings.body: `readLength()` returns -1 for the indefinite-length encoding (0x80). In `readInteger()` (line 71-72) and `readNext()` that value is passed straight to `read(int length)`, which does `new byte[length]` and will throw an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException on malformed/attacker-supplied DER instead of the declared IOException. Callers parsing untrusted signatures (asn1derToConcatenatedRS) would get an unexpected runtime exception. Reject indefinite length explicitly with an IOException.

findings.title: Dead code: two ASN1Encoder instances created and discarded
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` / `...write(sBigInteger)` and discard the results; the actual DER sequence is built again on lines 117-121. These two statements have no effect and should be removed to avoid confusing readers into thinking state is accumulated.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns an unrelated provider
findings.body: The method returns the provider of the default KeyStore type (e.g. SUN), which is not a BouncyCastle provider. Code paths such as BouncyIntegration/Provider-name based `getInstance(alg, provider)` lookups will silently use a provider that does not implement the expected algorithms, producing confusing NoSuchAlgorithmException errors far from the cause. Returning null or throwing UnsupportedOperationException (consistent with the other unimplemented methods) would be clearer.

findings.title: Test uses a default (P-256) EC key for ES384/ES512 cases
findings.body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the JDK default curve (typically secp256r1) for all three tests, so testES384/testES512 never exercise real P-384/P-521 signatures; r/s are just zero-padded to the larger length. Initialize the generator with the matching `ECGenParameterSpec` per algorithm so the conversion is validated for real ES384/ES512 signature sizes.
